title: Cloud Sync setup
summary: Diceroll's Cloud Sync page, Setup tab: storage per player as the pkey.cloudSync.bytes entitlement (the platform default plus tier values, with players near each limit), what syncs read from the catalog, the per-product ceiling, the platform writes-paused switch, and the saves code.
compare: One page replaces the old read-only Data page: Cloud Sync in the sidebar with Setup and Usage tabs. The sidebar shows Diceroll's six features in canonical order (Licensing, Managed config, Ship builds, Sign-in, Cloud Sync, Commerce) with Sign-in on because Cloud Sync needs it. The page sub is live state only: Verified per platform as status text, including "itch.io not seen yet" with the dashed ring (no description restating the title).

Storage per player is the only quota: the Default row is the platform's registry default (256 MiB), marked with the Platform pill and "For tiers that don't set their own"; one row per tier with its own value, or "Uses the default" under the value; players without a license show "Same as Free". No by-tier, by-entitlement or unlicensed settings, and no Set by column repeating the row's name.

One action style in the column, ghost buttons on one right edge: Change on rows with their own value, Set where the tier uses the default, Change… on Default (it opens config.storage-default, the live platform default confirm), and Change in Access for players without a license. On a narrow card each row's action sits beside its title.

The card names the entitlement once (pkey.cloudSync.bytes) and links to Tiers, where the same value is edited. Over 80% full is warning text only where it needs attention; the foot says, one line each, that lowering a limit deletes nothing and that new saves wait for room, with See Usage.

What syncs is read from the catalog (version named, Open Catalog): settings sync because they're Editable, with the count, the first keys, the two that stay on each device, and keys the game adds itself, with their limits as rows under it (Keys per player: up to 256; Size per player: up to 64 KiB).

Saves is the saves template (a neutral pill): slots, size, kept versions with "Older versions count toward the player's storage", the conflict rule in words (Ask the player), what the load screen shows, who can save, and one real slot.

Product limits has exactly two controls: Diceroll's total storage (a meter, '18.4 GiB of 50 GiB' and 'Platform default' on their own lines, Change…) and Pause all writes, marked Platform, off, with what it does in two lines; turning it on opens config.pause-writes. Limits and In your game sit side by side, each at its own height.

In your game: no sub-line and no comment narrating the code; GDScript first for Godot (then Swift for iOS, Kotlin for Android): config.set_value for a synced setting and cloud_sync.saves for a save with its metadata and the conflict signal.
A member with a product role only sees config.cloud-sync-product-role; while writes are paused the page is config.cloud-sync-paused.

Words: "player" for a game (Diceroll), "person" or "account" for an app (DJDL); storage in MiB and GiB, never MB; numbers and units never break across lines. products.integration's Cloud Sync card must say "Storage per person: 256 MiB by default (Standard uses the default)" to match this page.
No word "Data" for this page, no access classes, no conflict-mode jargon (lastWrite, revision) and no save-slot setting.
Phone: each tier row becomes a block with its action beside the title, the What syncs panes stack, and the code tabs scroll sideways. Page-level cards carry no decorative icon tile.

Wide (1600px and up): the page is two columns. Storage per player, What syncs and In your game take the main column; Limits, the operator's block, is the 400px aside. Below 1600 In your game and Limits sit side by side about 2:1, a section gap apart, and stack on phone.
Spacing and copy pass (2026-10-08): the screen sets no spacing of its own (kit primitives only), and each fact shows once, where it's most useful.

Brand v2 shell (lead B2–B5, 2026-10-09): the work sits on the inset canvas with a 3px rule in the page's context accent (full-bleed below 1024); one orientation line (context chip + crumbs, never 'Platform' on a product page, no eyebrow repeating the path); h1 36/44 on a collection, 32/40 on a record, 24/32 on a phone; the one filled primary is ink and selection is ink, the accent marks context only; the selected nav item is the subtle fill with a 3px marker; card heads are bands with no numerals; route tabs are an underline tablist with a 3px indicator; tables with filters are one workbench band; weights 400/500/600.

Masthead mark (B4): from 1024px a 48px flat tile on this page (the feature's glyph on a landing page, the product's icon on a product page) replaces the orientation chip; below 1024 the chip carries the context; never on a dense data page, a record or a state page.
Preserved (guide Ed. 04): Usage, policy and write controls stay separate decisions
Preserved (guide Ed. 04): Quota is per tier through the entitlement
Preserved (guide Ed. 04): Identity binding and product scope are shown
Preserved (guide Ed. 04): The global write-pause names its consequences

designReview.reviewer: UX designer (visual critique of rendered screenshots)
designReview.verdict: Fixed: the platform default is marked and confirmed like one, the actions agree, and the copy, Verified line and layout are corrected.

findings.issue: Change on the Default row edited the platform-wide 256 MiB default with no Platform marking and no confirm naming the products it affects.
findings.resolution: The row carries the Platform pill and reads "Every product, for people whose tier doesn't set it"; Change… opens ST-16's live platform default confirm, drawn as config.storage-default, which names DJDL and Diceroll with who uses the default in each and confirms with a passkey.

findings.issue: Four action treatments in one column (outline, pencil, text Set, nothing).
findings.resolution: One ghost style: Change on rows with their own value, Set on Standard (uses the default), Change… on Default, and Change in Access as a link on players without a license.

findings.issue: "Anonymous devices tier (Free)" read like a second tier or a price, with no way to change it.
findings.resolution: "Same as Free, the tier for players without a license" with Change in Access.

findings.issue: "Settings need no code" sat above code that calls set_value.
findings.resolution: "Settings sync with no extra code. Saves take one call."

findings.issue: The Verified line left out itch.io.
findings.resolution: The page sub adds "itch.io not seen yet" as muted status with the dashed ring, the products.integration pattern; config.cloud-sync-usage shows it too.

findings.issue: It never said whether kept versions count toward storage or what a player sees at the limit.
findings.resolution: Keeps adds "Older versions count toward the player's storage."; the card foot links "What players see then".

findings.issue: Ragged bottom row, a floating Platform pill and cut code tabs on phone, and "64 KiB" breaking.
findings.resolution: Limits and In your game stretch to one row height; on phone the pill has its own line and the tabs scroll with a fading edge; numbers and units are joined by non-breaking spaces.

findings.issue: No state for a member with a product role only.
findings.resolution: Added config.cloud-sync-product-role: Change… on Default and the pause switch are disabled, each with "Only platform admins …".

findings.issue: products.integration's DJDL card contradicts this page's storage model and uses MB.
findings.resolution: Not changed here, as the finding says: the fix belongs to products.integration, another designer's screen, and goes to the lead to route. The naming and unit rule is now in this screen's compare list.

findings.issue: Limits stretched to the Diceroll "In your game" row, leaving about 170px dead under the Pause switch; wide stretched the table.
findings.resolution: Pair is .mk-pair.loose.top (align-items start) so Limits keeps its height; at 1600+ it is the right rail beside Storage and What syncs.

findings.issue: Facts stated twice or mechanism the person does not act on.
findings.resolution: Storage subtitle "Per tier. Entitlement pkey.cloudSync.bytes"; Default subtitle "For tiers that don't set their own" with the Platform pill kept; removed the code-card footer, the "Every Editable setting syncs" sentence, the first code comment and "Last used Sep 22, for 14 min"; pause helper shortened; "What players see" became "See Usage"; "13 sync" became "13 settings".

findings.issue: "Updated 2 min ago" had no role and the header ran about 90px taller than other pages.
findings.resolution: Removed it; Guide stays right in the title row; verification stays in the title meta only; tab-bar gap tightened by the kit (.kit-cfg .page-head + .tabs).

findings.issue: Row actions sat about 40px inside the card edge; labels and blank cells were inconsistent.
findings.resolution: Ghost actions in rows and card heads are inset (-12px) so label text ends at the 24px edge; Change... only where a dialog opens; blank cell is an em dash; "players with data" removed from Setup rows (Usage owns the counts); column header is "Near limit" in both tabs.

findings.issue: Phone: clipped code tabs, orphaned Guide button, Pause (the urgent control) last.
findings.resolution: Code tabs show the language only and scroll with a fade, code block scrolls sideways with a fade, Guide is icon-only; Limits (Pause row first) comes directly under the header. Partly done: Guide still renders on its own row under the meta on phone (the kit phone page-actions rule wins over a screen override), not in the title row.

findings.issue: What syncs used three list styles with dead space under Settings.
findings.resolution: Both columns align to start; the two icon lines use one 20px icon column and a 12px gap.

findings.issue: Reword players/people/devices across the area; sentence-case eyebrows (UX2)
findings.resolution: declined: The house copy rules already distinguish these; uppercase eyebrows are a kit pattern. Only stray places fixed; no global rewrite.
